So I think the project started off with the goal of tying, if a model is making a specific decision, it should be based on facts and those facts should be presented as explanations. But then when they conducted the study, you the initial pilot study, they found that judging the presence of something in an object, so for example, one scenario that we had was we had a picture of a bowl of cereal.

segments.speaker: Aparna Balagopalan
segments.text: And if you ask lots of annotators, does this bowl of cereal have high sugar content, a majority of them said that it did. So that was just a factual question. So if you ask a different set of annotators, we have a school meal policy that prohibits meals with high sugar content. Now does this bowl of cereal have violated the school's meal policy, that is violated if there is high sugar content? And here only a small proportion of annotators said that the school meal policy was violated, which means that a fewer proportion of them thought that it contained high sugar content. So there was some difference in the way that annotators were judging facts versus norms.
